cues.zh: 我想今天我们可以聊聊“grep”，UNIX世界里一个众所周知的命令。它早在
cues.en: I thought today maybe we would talk about 'grep', a well-known command in the UNIX world. Something that's been around since the early

cues.zh: 1970年代初就已存在。“grep”让你能做的是搜索文本模式——任意的文本模式，在
cues.en: 1970s. What 'grep' lets you do is to search for patterns of text - arbitrary patterns of text in

cues.zh: 一个或多个文件中，而且输入文件的数量可以无限多。
cues.en: one or more files and there could be an unbounded number of

cues.zh: 或者输入也可以来自其他
cues.en: files of input. Or the input could be coming from some other

cues.zh: 程序，比如使用Unix管道时就是这样。
cues.en: program, for example as it is if you're using Unix pipelines.

cues.zh: 所以你拿某个程序，把它通过管道传给“grep”，这样一来，无论输入量有多大，“grep”都能
cues.en: So you take some program and you pipe it into 'grep' and that way, no matter what the amount of input is, 'grep' can

cues.zh: 筛选出，或展示给你，你感兴趣的内容。
cues.en: filter out, or show you, the things that you're interested in.

cues.zh: 而这是用文本编辑器很难方便做到的——甚至根本做不到。
cues.en: And that's stuff that you can't do with a text editor very conveniently - if at all.

cues.zh: “grep”一直以来的一个问题就是：
cues.en: One of the issues with 'grep' has always been:

cues.zh: 这个奇怪的名字到底从何而来？
cues.en: Where does that weird name come from?

cues.zh: 于是我想，也许我可以讲讲那个故事，如果大家感兴趣的话，我们就看看接下来会聊到哪里。
cues.en: And so I thought, perhaps, I could tell that story, if it would be of any interest and we'll see where we go from there.

cues.zh: 事情的由来是这样的——你得把自己带回到计算机的早期，在座所有人
cues.en: The way it came about - you have to put yourself back in the early days of computing, before everybody present in this room,

cues.zh: 除了我，都还没出生的那个年代。
cues.en: except me, was born.

cues.zh: 大概是
cues.en: Let's say something like

cues.zh: 1970到71年——UNIX非常非常早期的日子。
cues.en: 1970-71 -- the very, very, early days of UNIX.

cues.zh: UNIX运行的计算机是PDP 11。那时候
cues.en: The computer that UNIX ran on was a PDP 11. At that point

cues.zh: 大概是11/20型号。那是一台计算能力非常非常有限的机器。运行速度不快。
cues.en: it was probably an 11/20. It was a machine that had very very little computing power. It didn't run very fast.

cues.zh: 它的内存也不多。
cues.en: It also didn't have very much memory.

cues.zh: 大概在32K左右，
cues.en: Probably something in the order of 32K,

cues.zh: 也许是64K字节，是64 K字节，不是兆字节。
cues.en: maybe 64K bytes and that's 64 Kbytes, not megabytes.

cues.zh: 二级存储也很小，你知道，就几兆字节的磁盘之类的。
cues.en: And very small secondary storage as well, you know a few megabytes of disk and things like that.

cues.zh: 所以，计算资源非常非常有限，这意味着UNIX早期的大量软件
cues.en: So, very very limited computing resources and that meant that a lot of the software that was in early days of UNIX

cues.zh: 往往相当简单直接。
cues.en: tended to be fairly simple and straightforward.

cues.zh: 而这不仅反映了硬件的相对“孱弱”，也反映了从事这项工作的人的个人品味，
cues.en: And, that reflected not only the sort of ... the relative 'wimpiness' of the hardware but also the personal tastes of the people doing the work,

cues.zh: 主要是Ken Thompson和Dennis Ritchie。
cues.en: primarily Ken Thompson and Dennis Ritchie.

cues.zh: 所以人们使用的标准程序之一，就是任何系统上的文本编辑器
cues.en: So one of the prop ... one of the standard programs that people use is the text editor on any system

cues.zh: UNIX的文本编辑器叫“ed”，它不是读作“edd”
cues.en: The UNIX text editor was called 'ed', and it's not pronounced 'edd'

cues.zh: 至少内行人不这么读，它读作“ee dee”。
cues.en: At least by those in the know, it's pronounced 'ee dee'.

cues.zh: 这是Ken Thompson写的
cues.en: And this was written by Ken Thompson

cues.zh: 而且我认为它基本上是一个精简版的
cues.en: and I think it was a, basically, stripped-down version of an

cues.zh: 叫QED的编辑器，Ken之前用过它，并在上面做了大量工作。
cues.en: editor called QED, which Ken had worked with and done a lot of work on earlier.

cues.zh: 所以它是一个非常小、简单、直接的
cues.en: So a very small, simple, straightforward

cues.zh: 编辑器，你要记住的是，在那个年代，除了
cues.en: editor and the thing that you have to remember is that, in those days, in addition

cues.zh: 你还没有真正的视频显示终端——
cues.en: you didn't have actual video display terminals -

cues.zh: 不是我们今天习惯的那种，甚至不是10年或20年前的那种。
cues.en: not of the sort that we're used to today, or even 10 or 20 years ago.

cues.zh: 但实际上所有的计算、所有的编辑等等，都是在纸上完成的
cues.en: But in fact all the computing, all of your editing and so on, was done on paper

cues.zh: 还记得纸吗？如果你放大到这里
cues.en: Remember paper? If you zoom down here

cues.zh: 你能看到纸！这意味着有很多东西试图尽量减少纸张的使用。
cues.en: you can see paper! This meant that there were a lot of things that tried to minimize the use of paper.

cues.zh: 这也意味着编辑器一次只处理一行，或者一次处理多行，
cues.en: It also meant that editors worked one line at a time, or multiple lines at a time,

cues.zh: 但没有光标定位，所以你无法在一行内移动。
cues.en: but there was no cursor addressing, so you couldn't move around within a line.

cues.zh: 所以“ed”文本编辑器反映了这种情况。
cues.en: And so the 'ed' text editor reflected that kind of thing.

cues.zh: 也许我应该快速看一下“ed”是什么样子的？所以“ed”的命令都是单字母命令。
cues.en: Maybe what I should do is just a quick look at what 'ed' looked like? so the commands for 'ed' were single-letter commands.

cues.zh: 比如，有个命令叫“p”，
cues.en: So, for example, there was a command called 'p',

cues.zh: 代表“print”；有个命令叫“d”，用来删除一行
cues.en: Which stood for 'print'; there was a command called 'd', which would delete a line

cues.zh: 有个命令叫“s”，稍微有点……意思是“substitute”，可以替换
cues.en: There was a command called 's', which took a little bit ... which said 'substitute' so you could change this

cues.zh: 比如把“ABC”换成“DEF”之类的。
cues.en: y'know, 'ABC' into 'DEF', or something like that.

cues.zh: 还有个“append”命令，就是“加点文本”，你可以加好几行，然后用某个东西结束。
cues.en: There was an 'append' command that simply said 'add some more text' and you could add a bunch of lines and then terminate it with something.

cues.zh: 当然，还有个“read”命令
cues.en: There was, of course, a 'read' command

cues.zh: 可以从文件里读取信息，还有个“write”命令
cues.en: so that you could read information from a file, and there was a 'write' command [so]

cues.zh: 可以把内容写回文件。还有几个类似的东西。这就是它的核心功能。
cues.en: that you could put it back in a file. a handful of other things like that. So that was the essence of what it did.

cues.zh: “ed”做得很好的一点是，这些命令默认作用于当前行
cues.en: One of the things that 'ed' did very nicely was that, OK, these apply by default to the current line

cues.zh: 但如果你想更具体地指定操作哪些行，该怎么办呢？
cues.en: But what do you do when you want to have more specification of what lines you're operating on?

cues.zh: 所以你可以这样写，比如“第1行到第10行打印”
cues.en: And so you could say things like 'line 1 to line 10 print'

cues.zh: 这样就会打印出前10行。10就是指那个。
cues.en: So, this would print the first to 10 lines. 10 was that.

cues.zh: 但假设你想打印文件中的所有行呢？
cues.en: But suppose you wanted to print all of the lines in the file?

cues.zh: 于是有了一个简写叫做“$”。所以，我可以说“1,$p”，这样就会打印出文件中的所有行。
cues.en: So there was a shorthand called '$'. So, I could say '1,$p' and that would print all of the lines in the file.

cues.zh: 或者我可以说：“哎呀！我想……我只想看看最后一行”。那么我可以说“$p”，这样就会
cues.en: Or I could say: "Gee! I wonder ... I just want to see the last line". So I could say '$p' and that would

cues.zh: 给我那一行。我甚至可以省略“p”，但那样也足够了。
cues.en: give me that. I could even elide the 'p', but that's good enough.

cues.zh: 或者我可以通过说“$d”来删除最后一行。或者我可以通过说“1d”来删除第一行。
cues.en: Or I could delete the last line by saying '$d'. Or I could delete the first line by saying '1d'.

cues.zh: 这就是所谓的行寻址。到目前为止还不太复杂。
cues.en: That is sort of the line addressing. So far not very complicated.

cues.zh: “ed”在此基础上增加的东西，而且这绝对是Ken的影响，就是正则表达式的概念。
cues.en: The thing that 'ed' added to all of that, and this is definitely Ken's influence was the idea of regular expressions.

cues.zh: 所以，正则表达式是一种文本模式
cues.en: So, a regular expression is a pattern of

cues.zh: 文本——它是一种指定文本模式的方式。
cues.en: text - its a way of specifying patterns of text.

cues.zh: 它们可以是像单词'print'这样的字面文本，也可以是更复杂的东西，比如以
cues.en: They could be literal texts like the word 'print' or they could be something more complicated, like things that start with

cues.zh: 'Prin'开头，但可能延伸为'Print'或'Princeton'或'Princess'之类的，诸如此类。
cues.en: 'Prin' and but might go on to 'Print' or 'Princeton' or 'Princess', or whatever, That kind of thing.

cues.zh: 而在'ed'文本编辑器中，正则表达式的写法是你输入'/'，然后
cues.en: And the way that regular expressions were written in the 'ed' text editor was you said '/' and

cues.zh: 写下正则表达式的字符。所以，我可以写'/print/'
cues.en: then you wrote the characters of the regular expression. So, I could say '/print/'

cues.zh: 那就会匹配我手头工作中下一行包含单词'print'的内容
cues.en: and that would be something that would match the next line, in what I was working on, that contained the word 'print'

cues.zh: 无论它出现在行内哪个位置。
cues.en: anywhere within it.

cues.zh: 所以'ed'编辑器中的正则表达式有些不同——比你在shell通配符中可能遇到的正则表达式
cues.en: eSo the regular expressions in the 'ed' editor were somewhat different - a little more

cues.zh: 更精巧、更复杂，
cues.en: sophisticated, and complicated, than the regular expressions that you might find in shell wildcards,

cues.zh: 比如在shell通配符里，星号意味着'任意内容'。所以，
cues.en: where, for example, a star means 'anything at all'. So,

cues.zh: 同样是文本模式的概念——但规格略有不同
cues.en: the same idea of patterns of text - a slightly different

cues.zh: 写法不同，但适合文本编辑。于是，我就可以说“我想找到文件中下一个
cues.en: specification - a different way of writing patterns but suitable for text editing. And so, then, I could say things like "I want to find the next

cues.zh: 出现的单词'print'”。然后我就定位到那里了。
cues.en: occurrence of the word 'print' in my file". And then there I would be.

cues.zh: 就这样一直下去，像那样。好，这就是“ed”文本编辑器。
cues.en: And on, and on, and on, like that. OK, so that's the 'ed' text editor.

cues.zh: 到这里，我们已经离“grep”很远了。那么“grep”到底是干什么的？
cues.en: We are a long way away from 'grep' at this point. So what's 'grep' all about?

cues.zh: 嗯，事实证明，在那个时期，“ed”是标准的文本编辑器。
cues.en: Well, it turns out that at the time that this was going on, 'ed' was the standard text editor.

cues.zh: 但是，就像我说的，你们用的机器非常非常弱。
cues.en: But, as I said, the machines you're working on are very very wimpy.

cues.zh: 在很多方面计算能力都不强
cues.en: Not much computing capacity in a lot of ways

cues.zh: 而事实上
cues.en: And in fact

cues.zh: 其中一个限制是你没法编辑非常大的文件，
cues.en: one of the limitations was that you couldn't edit a very big file,

cues.zh: 因为内存不够，而“ed”完全在内存里工作，
cues.en: because there wasn't enough memory and the 'ed' worked entirely within memory and

cues.zh: 所以你就卡住了。我当时的一位同事，Lee McMahon，对做文本
cues.en: so you were stuck. One of my colleagues at the time, Lee McMahon, was very interested in doing text

cues.zh: 分析非常感兴趣。就是那种我们今天也许称之为
cues.en: analysis. The sort of thing that we would call today,

cues.zh: 自然语言处理的东西。
cues.en: perhaps, Natural Language Processing.

cues.zh: 所以 Lee 想做的事……他一直在研究
cues.en: And so what Lee wanted to do ... he had been studying

cues.zh: 一个当时非常有趣的问题：一些被称为《联邦党人文集》的
cues.en: something that, at the time, was the very interesting question of who were the authors of

cues.zh: 美国基础文献的作者到底是谁。《联邦党人文集》是由
cues.en: some fundamental American documents called the Federalist Papers. The Federalist Papers were written by,

cues.zh: James Madison、Alexander Hamilton 和 John Jay 在
cues.en: variously, James Madison and Alexander Hamilton and John Jay in

cues.zh: 1787 年和 88 年分别撰写的，如果我没记错的话。这些文献共有 85 篇
cues.en: 1787 and 88, if I recall correctly, There were 85 of these documents

cues.zh: 但它们是以 Publius 这个笔名匿名发表的。所以理论上我们根本不知道是谁写的
cues.en: But they were published anonymously under the name Publius. And so we had no idea, in theory, who wrote them

cues.zh: 因此有大量学术研究试图确切弄清楚。
cues.en: And so there's been a lot of scholarship trying to figure out for sure.

cues.zh: 众所周知，其中一些文章的作者已经明确，而另一些我认为
cues.en: It's well known who wrote some of them and others are still, I think, a

cues.zh: 还不太确定，所以 Lee 有兴趣看看你能否实际上，
cues.en: little uncertain and so Lee was interested in seeing whether you could actually,

cues.zh: 通过他自己设计的文本分析，
cues.en: by textual analysis of his own devising,

cues.zh: 弄清楚这些文章是谁写的。这没问题。但事实证明，这 85 份文档总共才刚过一兆字节
cues.en: figure out who wrote these things. So that's fine. But it turns out that these 85 documents was in total just over a megabyte

cues.zh: ——我的意思是按今天的标准这微不足道——根本放不下。他没法在 'ed' 里把它们全部编辑。
cues.en: - I mean down in the noise by today's standards - wouldn't fit. He couldn't edit them all in 'ed'.

cues.zh: 那怎么办呢？
cues.en: And so what do you do?

cues.zh: 有一天他说：“我只想通读一遍，找出《联邦党人文集》中所有出现‘某词’的地方
cues.en: So one day he said: "I just want to go through and find all the occurrences of 'something' in the Federalist Papers

cues.zh: 好让我看看！”他把这话对 Ken Thompson 说了，然后
cues.en: so I can look at 'em!" And he said this to Ken Thompson and

cues.zh: 就回家吃晚饭什么的。第二天他回来时，Ken 已经写好了程序——
cues.en: then went home for dinner or something like that. And he came back the next day and Ken had written the program -

cues.zh: 这个程序叫 'grep'。'grep' 所做的是遍历
cues.en: and the program was called 'grep'. And what 'grep' did was to go through a

cues.zh: 一堆文档——一个或多个文件——然后
cues.en: bunch of documents - one or more files - and

cues.zh: 简单地找出某个特定正则表达式在这些文档中出现过的所有位置。
cues.en: simply find all of the places where a particular regular expression appeared in those things.

cues.zh: 于是……结果发现 'ed' 里还有一个命令叫 'g'。它代表“全局”。
cues.en: And so the way ... it turns out that one more of the commands in 'ed' is a command called 'g'. And this stood for 'global'.

cues.zh: 它的意思是，对每一行匹配某个正则表达式的行——
cues.en: And what it said was, on every line that matches a particular regular expression -

cues.zh: 比如 'print'——我就可以执行一个 'ed' 命令，我可以说：“在每一行包含 'print' 这个词的行上
cues.en: so, for example,'print'- I can then do an 'ed' command So, I could say: "On every line that contains the word 'print'

cues.zh: 我就把它打印出来”。这样我就能看到我那些 print 语句长什么样。
cues.en: I'll just print it". So, I can see what my various print statements would look like.

cues.zh: 或者我可以用另一种方式，说 'g'——里面放另一个正则表达式——然后把它们删掉。这样我就能删掉程序中所有的
cues.en: Or I could, in some other way, say 'g' - and some other regular expression in there - and delete them. So I could delete all of the

cues.zh: 注释之类的东西。
cues.en: comments in a program, or something like that.

cues.zh: 所以它的总体结构就是 'g' 后面跟着（在斜杠里）一个正则表达式，
cues.en: So the general structure of that is 'g' followed by (in slashes), a regular expression,

cues.zh: 再跟着字母 'p'——g/re/p——这就是它名字的由来。
cues.en: followed by the letter 'p' - g/re/p - and that's the genesis of where it came from.

cues.zh: 从某种意义上说，这就是 Ken Thompson 的天才之处。一个漂亮的程序，转眼间就写好了，办法是拿
cues.en: OK, and so this is in some ways the genius of Ken Thompson. A beautiful program, written in no time at all, by taking some

cues.zh: 另一个程序来修剪一番，然后给它起个叫得响的名字。这就是 'grep' 的由来。
cues.en: other program and just trimming it out and then giving it a name that stuck. That's the story of where 'grep' came from.

cues.zh: 我再补充一点——25 年前，那正是 1993 年春天，
cues.en: Let me add one thing - 25 years ago [it] literally was the spring of 1993,

cues.zh: 我当时作为访问学者在普林斯顿教书。
cues.en: I was teaching at Princeton as a visitor.

cues.zh: 我需要给我的编程课布置一个作业。然后我想：“嗯！”
cues.en: And I needed an assignment for my programming class. And I thought "Hmm!"

cues.zh: 于是我告诉班上的学生：“好，这是 'ed' 的源代码。”
cues.en: So what I did was to tell them - the students in the class: "OK, here is the source code for 'ed' "

cues.zh: 当时它大概有
cues.en: It was at that time probably

cues.zh: 1800 行 C 代码。
cues.en: 1800 lines of C.

cues.zh: “你们的任务是把这 1800 行 C 代码改写成 'grep' 这个 C 程序。
cues.en: "Your job is to take these 1800 lines of C and convert them into 'grep' as a C program.

cues.zh: 好，给你们一周时间完成。”
cues.en: OK, and you've got a week to do it".

cues.zh: 然后我告诉他们，他们有几个优势。第一，
cues.en: And I told them, at that point, that they had a couple of advantages. First,

cues.zh: 他们知道目标是什么。
cues.en: they knew what the target was.

cues.zh: 有人已经做过'grep'，所以他们知道它应该是什么样子。他们只需复制那种行为。
cues.en: Somebody had already done 'grep' so they knew what it was supposed to look like. And all they had to do was replicate that behavior.

cues.zh: 另一件事是，它现在是用C语言编写的。最初的'grep'是用PDP 11汇编语言编写的。
cues.en: And the other thing is that it was now written in C. The original 'grep' was written in PDP 11 assembly language.

cues.zh: 当然，他们也有一个严重的劣势：他们都不是Ken Thompson。
cues.en: And of course, they also had one grave disadvantage: None of them were Ken Thompson.
